laws.rule: EU drone rules do not apply in New Caledonia; local rules do. Leisure flying generally needs no authorisation or declaration from DAC-NC. Outside restricted zones the maximum height is 120 m. Restricted areas are on the GEOREP map, which does not show temporary bans; some lagoon islets may be closed to people and drone overflight to protect seabirds (check with Province Sud). The old duty to declare aerial image capture has been repealed.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Outside of tourist areas, dress and behaviour standards are conservative. Take care not to offend. Visits to certain areas, including popular fishing and maritime areas, may require prior authorisation from the relevant customary authorities. This is carried out through engaging in a 'coutume' (customary acknowledgement gesture). Check with local authorities or your travel operator to determine when this is appropriate. New Caledonia Tourism - Traditions, Customs and Etiquette (in English) New Caledonia Tourism: when entering customary land or visiting a Kanak tribe without a pre-arranged stay, make the customary gesture. Present a small gift (traditionally cloth and a 500 XPF note) to the chief with a few words.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Pacific Franc (XPF). Declare all amounts over 10,000 euros (or equivalent) on arrival and departure. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. Australian dollars are accepted by some businesses. Change Australian dollars for XPF at banks and authorised exchange bureaus. There are ATMs and credit card facilities in Noumea and other major centres. Take enough cash in XPF if you're travelling to more remote areas. New Caledonia Currency | New Caledonia Tourism & Travel (in English)

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: New Caledonia's civil aviation directorate (DAC-NC) requires professional drone activity to be declared beforehand, and is moving to the EU framework. Leisure flying generally needs no authorisation. No public operator register or visitor rule was found.

items.text: No public register of professional drone operators was found on the DAC-NC pages read.

Any professional activity by a remote-aircraft operator is subject to prior declaration (through the Alpha Tango platform for EU standard scenarios STS-01 and STS-02; for national scenarios S1 to S3, email DAC-NC first). Flights over 2 kg under S2 or S3 need a design attestation, or the alternative specific authorisations the authority publishes (NC-2024-01 to 03 and NC-AS-2026-01). Pilot training is described on its licences and examinations page.

Not stated: the page does not address foreign operators or foreign-registered drones, and refers questions to DAC-NC. Importing a drone needs the radio import authorisation (AAI) from the ANFR unless the model is exempt.

Restricted zones are on the GEOREP map (ncdrones.georep.nc), which does not show temporary bans. Professional operators can request authorisation for restricted zones. Zones banned for capturing aerial data are set by an arrete of 26 June 2024.
